bottleneck: Mapping all 86 billion neurons and ~100 trillion synapses of a human brain at synaptic resolution is not technically feasible today: imaging a single cubic millimeter takes years, reconstruction algorithms are costly, and storing the full dataset would require roughly a zettabyte. The mouse brain — the realistic next target — is itself a decade-scale project. A human connectome at current costs would run tens of billions of dollars.
current_state: Complete connectomes exist only for tiny nervous systems (C. elegans, fruit fly larva). Mammalian whole-brain mapping awaits 10,000-fold cost reductions per neuron.

sources.title: The Human Connectome: A Structural Description of the Human Brain

title: Human connectome mapping technically infeasible today
why_it_blocks: You cannot fix what you cannot map. Without a human wiring diagram, circuit-level understanding of neurological and psychiatric disease stays out of reach.
